answer: Shared-Secret Lotus Split. Each agent identity is issued a secret split into k shares, one planted in a distinct harbor of the registry's record graph; a duplicate identity must reconstruct the same shares, and the graph flags any two records resolving to one secret. Duplication therefore forces re-derivation and re-planting across k independent records, costing the attacker k storage and verification operations per fake identity, while honest agents pay once. The vine of references tying shares together makes silent copying infeasible.
